preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(prices) == n and all(0 <= c <= 10**9 for c in prices)
preconditions.description: There are exactly n non-negative integer prices, each at most 10^9.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n for a, b in edges)
preconditions.description: There are exactly n-1 edges connecting vertices within the valid range [1, n].
The edges form a valid tree rooted at vertex 1.

postconditions.description: The first output integer min_cost is the minimum total cost required to guarantee a win.
The second output integer k is the count of vertices belonging to at least one optimal set.

postconditions.expression: optimal_vertices == sorted([v for v in range(1, n+1) if exists_optimal_set_containing(v, prices, edges, n, min_cost)])
postconditions.description: The list of vertices contains exactly those indices that appear in at least one optimal set, sorted in increasing order.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n for v in optimal_vertices) and len(set(optimal_vertices)) == len(optimal_vertices)
postconditions.description: All listed vertices are distinct and within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0].split() == [str(min_cost), str(k)] and output_lines[1].split() == [str(v) for v in optimal_vertices]
postconditions.description: The output format matches the specification: first line has cost and count, second line has the sorted vertex indices.
